tools.name: tdev_workspace
tools.description: Create, list and inspect development spaces; attach/detach enrolled projects, configure defaults and close. Membership selects projects, never grants authority. Empty spaces need no Git repository. Mutations use expectedRevision; close/detach retain source tasks and owned branches and require no open or uncertain tasks. Omit workspaceId when starting a task to use an automatic default space.

tools.name: tdev_task
tools.description: Start, inspect and manage an isolated source task for one project in a workspace. Start resolves project/base HEAD and owned branch naming. Omit workspaceId for an automatic default workspace; explicit workspaces use attached projects and their defaultRepo. Edit source with tdev_edit. Close retains branches; cleanup removes only an unchanged branch owned by this task. Continue a proved publication via start.fromTaskId. Start with localChanges=true to import the enrolled local checkout without writing to it. Integrate another same-project task delta with three-way merging; applied=false means the target is unchanged. Retry conflict resolution with new requestId and the returned sourceCheckpoint; keep prior resolutions if conflicts are truncated. Inspect includes outstanding processes independent of history pagination and dependency storage. resetEnvironment removes task dependencies/caches only after every execution is proved stopped; it also works after close. Close retains processes and dependencies.

localChanges.description: Capture the enrolled checkout final working-tree bytes into a new task; preserve its index/files/refs. Requires a matching checked-out source branch.

tools.name: tdev_read
tools.description: Batch bounded immutable file/list/literal-search/diff/history reads at a checkpoint. Omit checkpoint to read the current committed task snapshot. Diff supports stat/patch/names, an accessible base checkpoint and byte pagination.

tools.name: tdev_edit
tools.description: Atomically edit files at expected checkpoint. Same request replays before stale checks.

tools.name: tdev_exec
tools.description: Run commands in the Termux-native development environment (same-UID developer authority, host network, not a sandbox). Returns a retained operation handle. For ordinary non-interactive ChatGPT Code Mode work, send waitMs=30000 so admission and one bounded terminal/log observation happen in the same nested tool call; omit it or set waitMs=0 for staged-stdin or immediate-handle workflows. If it still returns running, continue with tdev_operation status without replaying the effect. waitMs is observation-only and does not change request identity; process mode ignores it and returns immediately. Never resubmit with a new request after response loss. Dependencies/caches persist per task through TDEV_ENV_DIR; use environment=fresh for a disposable environment. mode=process starts a foreground development server/debugger on a fixed checkpoint without blocking source edits or capturing its files; omit timeout to run until cancel/exit. Observe later logs/stdin/cancel/retire through tdev_operation.

waitMs.description: Bounded terminal observation after command admission. Omit or set 0 for an immediate retained handle; set a positive value to wait up to this many milliseconds for the exact admitted operation and return the freshest status/log page. This observation-only field does not change mutation identity and is ignored for process mode. On MCP HTTP, a positive command wait with _meta.progressToken uses request-scoped SSE with standard progress notifications; without progressToken the bounded wait returns one application/json response.

mode.description: command captures stopped source and defaults to 300s. Native process keeps a fixed source copy, permits task edits, never captures source and runs until stop/exit unless timeout is supplied.

environment.description: Default task reuses the task's private dependency/cache storage; fresh uses only this operation. HOME and source remain per-operation.

tools.name: tdev_operation
tools.description: Inspect any accepted operation by operationId or original request ID, including project and workspace changes. Status observes current progress without repeating effects. For exec/validation processes only: deliver sequenced stdin, request cancellation or retire stopped resources. ChatGPT Code Mode caller guidance (not a server limit): use short physical functions.exec cells, conservatively at most 16 total nested attempts including failures and diagnostics, and check a soft 15-second elapsed budget before another ordinary call. Reserve closing markers within that budget. For one already-admitted ongoing exec/validation/build, use the operation-monitor exception: keep the exact identity and perform one read-only status call with waitMs (at most 30000) per physical cell, advancing the returned output cursor and never replaying the effect. This reduces dependence on host scheduling a fresh physical cell every 30 seconds and surfaces terminal failed/cancelled state before return. If the in-cell monitor budget ends while still running, return exact continuation state and end the cell normally; after receiving it, the assistant reports progress and issues a fresh functions.exec in the same turn without waiting for user input unless blocked or interrupted. Unknown, malformed, unavailable or ambiguous results stop for review/reconciliation of the original identity. Never retry ambiguous effects or regenerate requestId; observe the original operation and never infer success from transport completion. These are adjustable caller defaults, not guaranteed host capabilities; server completion and markers do not prove visible UI delivery.

waitMs.description: Bounded read-only terminal wait. While the operation is running or unknown, status waits up to this many milliseconds for terminal reconciliation, then returns the freshest status/log page; nonterminal log growth does not end the wait. On MCP HTTP, a positive wait with _meta.progressToken uses request-scoped SSE with standard progress notifications; without progressToken the bounded wait returns one application/json response. Omission or 0 remains an immediate JSON response.

tools.name: tdev_validate
tools.description: Freeze an exact candidate commit and run the operator's mandatory command through trusted outer execution. For ordinary ChatGPT Code Mode source validation, send waitMs=30000 so admission and one bounded terminal/log observation happen in the same nested tool call; omit it or set waitMs=0 when an immediate retained handle is required. If it still returns running, continue with tdev_operation status without replaying the effect. waitMs is observation-only and does not change request identity. With subject=artifact and artifactId, verifies retained bytes using adopted artifactValidation policy in fresh scratch; never alters source. Service packages additionally require a free loopback health port/path and exercise the manifest entrypoint with TDEV_PORT and X-Tdev-Release. Observe later logs/cancel/retire through tdev_operation. Artifact validation cannot authorize source publication.

environment.description: Default task reuses the task's private dependency/cache storage; fresh uses only this operation. HOME and source remain per-operation.

timeout.description: Validation deadline in seconds; default 300. Increase for a longer adopted test suite, up to 3600.

waitMs.description: Bounded terminal observation after source-validation admission. Omit or set 0 for an immediate retained handle; set a positive value to wait up to this many milliseconds for the exact admitted validation and return the freshest status/log page. This observation-only field does not change mutation identity. On MCP HTTP, a positive source-validation wait with _meta.progressToken uses request-scoped SSE with standard progress notifications; without progressToken the bounded wait returns one application/json response.

health.description: Readiness requires HTTP 200 from 127.0.0.1:port/path with X-Tdev-Release equal to the process TDEV_RELEASE environment value.

timeout.description: Validation deadline in seconds; default 300. Increase for a longer adopted test suite, up to 3600.

tools.name: tdev_publish
tools.description: Publish exactly the validated commit. Expected remote state is derived from its task when omitted; managed tasks create their branch only on first publication. Provider authentication belongs to the controller, not tdev_exec.

tools.name: tdev_project
tools.description: List projects and delegated policies; connect existing local Git folders or GitHub repositories, or create initialized projects. Local names are relative to the policy root; GitHub names are repository names under the policy owner. GitHub creation is private. Uses controller provider credentials; no gh authentication in exec needed. No caller-supplied credentials, commands or executor settings. Inspect original mutations through tdev_operation status.

tools.name: tdev_deploy
tools.description: Deploy a successfully validated native source candidate to a delegated Termux runit target. Release creates/updates a named owned service and checks process identity plus configured loopback HTTP readiness. Inspect returns current state and rotating logs; start/stop/rollback/remove require revision CAS. Remove preserves data/releases/logs. Observe interrupted effects through tdev_operation status before retrying. Source publication is separate; task dependency directories are not bundled. The app must return HTTP 200 with X-Tdev-Release equal to TDEV_RELEASE; writable state belongs in TDEV_DATA_DIR. Services must stay in the foreground. release subject=artifact uses a successful artifact validationId and manifest launch settings; command override is forbidden. health.port is the deployment port supplied as TDEV_PORT; health.path must match validation. Current artifact/runtime/policy checks precede stopping the previous service.

expectedRevision.description: Supply the inspected revision for an update. Omitted resolves the current revision during admission; concurrent changes are still checked.

command.description: Foreground command in the exact source release; use TDEV_DATA_DIR for persistent writable data. Task venv/cache and build outputs are not packaged.

health.description: Readiness requires HTTP 200 from 127.0.0.1:port/path with X-Tdev-Release equal to the process TDEV_RELEASE environment value.

expectedRevision.description: Supply the inspected revision for an update. Omitted resolves the current revision during admission; concurrent changes are still checked.

health.description: Readiness requires HTTP 200 from 127.0.0.1:port/path with X-Tdev-Release equal to the process TDEV_RELEASE environment value.

tools.name: tdev_artifact
tools.description: Inspect a recipe from successful source validation, prepare a retained native build, list builds or inspect sealed bytes. Default recipe path: tdev-package.json. prepare requires requestId and validationId; reuse the request after a lost reply. Uses fresh source, pinned public HTTPS dependencies and declared exports, independent of task caches and deployment targets. Observe/log/cancel/retire through tdev_operation; artifactId is the build operation id. list exposes outstanding builds regardless of history page. Build success is not artifact validation or deployment. Use tdev_validate subject=artifact for verification. Service inspect reports current declared runtime compatibility separately from retained-byte integrity; it never installs or starts a service. Export reads verified file bytes in bounded base64 pages, never writes caller paths. usage returns paged authorized retained-object counts, excluding scratch and deployment copies; shared digests can recur across pages. prunePreview reports live pins and retention policy; explicit prune requires its token and rechecks pins, journals retirement and preserves historical receipts. Active/previous deployments and unknown work cannot be pruned. No automatic GC.

path.description: Canonical relative path; no traversal, backslashes, control characters or .git components. Additional path/overlap checks are enforced by the controller.

tools.name: tdev_diagnostics
tools.description: Observe optional runtime diagnostics. inspect view=summary returns principal-scoped server error counts, separately counted client reports, pending and retry-exhausted incidents in one bounded response; default full also includes up to 32 incidents. report with a stable requestId and a category records a client-observed visible stall, transport error, call limit, unexpected turn end or control mismatch and starts a bounded capture; this is a report, not server/UI proof. Never include raw error messages, commands, auth or conversation text. Reuse requestId after a lost report/activation reply within retained history. activate starts a bounded trace; stop ends capture, not development work. report/activate/stop require the diagnostic grant. Acknowledge a received incidentId once; inspect remains available after automatic offers are exhausted. Notifications use fair selection, exponential backoff and at most eight offers per incident; failed writes do not acknowledge delivery. Counters are best effort, bounded and restart-persisted, not a complete audit. No retry/cancel/provider mutation, host wake-up or UI-delivery guarantee. mark requires the diagnostic grant and watch/trace; it records bounded caller execution witnesses without activating capture. Read inspect.witness.instance first; use fresh opaque hex run/cell IDs and increasing run sequence. tool_return requires callOrdinal and may reference the preceding response diagnosticReceipt.request as afterRequest. Marker arrival is caller assertion, not UI proof; mark failures must not retry/cancel development work. Reuse identical instance/runId/sequence only for a lost marker reply, within bounded process-local retention.

oneOf.description: Opt-in caller witness, not host attestation or UI proof. Identity is principal + instance + runId + sequence (no operational requestId). Sequence strictly increases per run, gaps allowed. Exact retained retry returns original receipt without another event; conflicting retained identity fails WITNESS_CONFLICT, old evicted sequence fails WITNESS_REPLAY_EXPIRED, stale instance fails WITNESS_INSTANCE_CHANGED. At most 32 runs per process and 256 cached receipts globally; run watermarks never evict, further new runs fail WITNESS_RUN_LIMIT. Off rejects without activation. Watch retains ring only; trace also queues bounded persistence. Never retry development work because marking failed. afterRequest is optional caller assertion referencing diagnosticReceipt.request from a returned response of the same instance; no validation of that prior response or claim of UI delivery.
